text:
micah: Quick thread — ok to bikeshed here but want a short decision or list of follow-ups. We need to pick a default pattern for private connectivity between customer VPCs and the control plane: per-tenant NATed private endpoints vs a regional relay/proxy layer.

micah: TL;DR: per-tenant endpoints give stable egress IPs and simpler network policies for customers, but multiply IP management and cross-account peering work. A regional relay centralizes egress and makes ops simpler but adds another hop and a termination boundary for TLS. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

tara: I lean relay for most customers. We already have relay infra for hosted paths and can extend it into Dedicated/Private with tight ACLs. Saves us from per-customer route table churn.

jonathan: Relay + mTLS between customer and relay would preserve security but we need a strong auth model. If relay terminates TLS for upstream control-plane connections we must ensure integrity (signed client certs, SNI pinning?)

amy: Curious about cost delta — relay increases egress bandwidth and instance count regionally. For low-volume tenants it's cheaper; for high-volume tenants the relay becomes a hotspot and we either autoscale or push them to a direct endpoint.

micah: Good point. Proposal: default to relay for onboarding simplicity. Offer an opt-in dedicated egress IP / per-customer endpoint for high-throughput or compliance customers. That lets us avoid per-tenant infra until needed.

devx: Would an opt-in add-on be toggle-able from Console + infra-as-code? Need a consistent API so SDKs can pick the right base URL.

jonathan: API-wise we should surface a connection_mode enum: ["relay", "direct", "hybrid"]. SDKs resolve URL+certs from a single endpoint: GET /tenants/:id/connection-info.

amy: Ops question: who owns the TLS termination model? If relay terminates, we need to rotate certs safely and provide audit logs. If direct keeps end-to-end TLS, we need to convince customers to accept our CA or use mutual TLS.

micah: For relay-mode we'll do relay-terminates + mTLS upstream to control plane. For direct-mode, prefer mutual TLS between customer agent and control-plane endpoint with optional NAT'ed IP allocation.

ops-oncall: For per-tenant endpoints we need automation to allocate /27s or use NAT gateway pools per account. Manual allocation won't scale. Also need egress IP preservation during failover.

amy: Could we use an ephemeral-Tunnel model? Customer agent opens an outbound mTLS tunnel to relay, relay maintains long-lived TCP to control plane. That preserves outbound-only firewall rules for customers and keeps us from asking them to allow inbound.

jonathan: Sketch of connection flows:
```
# relay-mode:
customer-agent -> mTLS -> regional-relay (terminate) -> mTLS -> control-plane

# direct-mode:
customer-agent -> mTLS -> control-plane (per-tenant endpoint / NAT)
```

tara: I like tunnel for most customers. Means we never require peering or cross-account routing. Also reduces AWS peering ops.

devx: UX notes: Console should show which mode tenant is in, current egress IPs (if direct) and a live path check. Also a "fail-open" policy: if relay unavailable, should we fallback to direct if configured?

micah: Fallback is useful but dangerous for private clouds. Maybe allow fallback only for non-compliant tenants; default is fail-closed. Put policy into tenant config.

sre-bot: deploy-bot: Relay autoscaler triggered: region-us-east-1 up by 3 instances (reason: spike in relay relays) :rocket:

amy: Action items I see:
  1) jonathan - draft auth model doc for relay vs direct (client certs, rotation, audit)
  2) ops-oncall - cost/infra spike model for relay autoscaling and per-tenant NAT pools
  3) devx - Console + API contract for connection_mode and /connection-info endpoint
  4) micah - write short RFC follow-up with recommended default: relay (tunnel) + opt-in direct per-tenant endpoints for high-throughput/compliant customers.

micah: Ok if we call this done for now? If no objections I'll put the follow-up RFC in docs and link here. :thumbsup:

tara: +1 from me.

jonathan: +1, will start auth doc today.

ops-oncall: +1, will sketch infra plan.

devx: +1, will draft API and Console mockups.

amy: +1.

micah: Cool — thanks all. Will create RFC and tag owners.
